name: Arch
summary: A curved head over an opening that carries load as compression; inside, a soft frame for a door, a mirror or a niche.
how: Use a semicircular head: the rise is half the span.
Keep the ratio of height to width of the opening at 1.6:1 to 2:1.
In a room, repeat the arch in 2 or 3 places, for example a door, a mirror and a niche, and no more.

origin.note: Roman builders use the semicircular masonry arch at large scale in aqueducts, bridges and gates; the arch itself is older.

adoptions.via: Palladian arched windows and niches frame Georgian rooms.
Postmodern facades quote the round arch as a sign, not as a structure.
Arched mirrors, headboards, doorways and painted arches become a room motif.

sources.title: John Summerson, The Classical Language of Architecture (1963)
